expl: Fertilization occurs at the end of the fallopian tube or oviduct away from the uterus (close to the ovary). The oviduct is the tube that links ovary to the uterus and ovulated oocyte travels down to become fertilized by sperm present in the female tract.

stem: In human beings, normally in which one of the following parts, does the sperm fertilize the ovum ?
expl: In human beings, normally the sperm fertilizes the ovum in the fallopian tube. Fallopian tube, also called oviduct or uterine tube, either of a pair of long narrow ducts located in the human female abdominal cavity that transport the male sperm cells to the egg, provide a suitable environment for fertilization and transport the egg from the ovary, where it is produced.

stem: After reaching the female genital tract, human sperms retain their fertilizing capacity for –
expl: A sperm remains alive for up to about 72 hours after entering into oviduct but its capacity to fertilize the ovum lasts for about 48 hours (2 days).

stem: The heart of human embryo starts beating?

options.label: a
options.text: In the first week of development

options.label: b
options.text: In the third week of its development

options.label: c
options.text: In the fourth week of its development

options.label: d
options.text: In the sixth week of its development

expl: About 4-5 weeks after fertilization, when the heart of human embryo first begins to beat, the sound of the little heart is too soft to hear. In 4-5 weeks, the heart of human embryo typically beats between about 105 to 121 times per minute.

stem: Which one of the following is a membrane that protects the developing embryo from desiccation ?
expl: The amnion is a membrane that covers the embryo. It is filled with the amniotic fluid which causes the amnion to expand and become the amniotic sac which serves to provide a protective environment for the developing embryo against desiccation, outer pressure etc.

stem: In which organ sertoli cells are found?
expl: Sertoli cells are somatic cells found in human testes which contribute to the process of spermatogenesis (the production of sperm) as a structural component of the seminiferous tubules. They are activated by follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) secreted by the adenohypophysis and express FSH receptor on their membranes. They are a type of sustentacular 'nurse' cell.
